leave_behind: REAL FINDING ABOUT THE WRITER, not just the composer: the land-use-fact ATOM WRITER is now known-permanently-behind the Tier-1 bake for both gate-blocked counties (Hays 48209, Williamson 48491). It has no address-join recovery mechanism of its own and, absent a change, never will -- it will keep writing/serving a join-hold absence for every node in LANDUSE_JOIN_DISABLED_FIPS_SEED even after this fix, on any node the bake has already (or will later) legitimately recover via situs-address match. This fix makes the BRIEF prefer the bake's recovered value over the atom, which is the right read-time behavior, but it does not correct the atom itself -- the atom remains wrong at its own source, and any OTHER consumer of the land-use-fact atom directly (not through r1BriefCompose.ts) will still see and could still act on the stale join-hold claim. The writer (land-use-fact-writer.ts per landUseFactRead.ts's own docstring) was not found inside legacy-design-tools by repo-wide grep -- it lives outside this dispatch's repo scope (likely hauska-engine). Whoever owns it should either (a) teach it the same owner-gated situs-address recovery buildTier1Payload already implements, or (b) have it re-evaluate/re-write against gate-blocked-county nodes once a bake has recovered a value, so the atom stops being a second, silently-wrong source of truth for every consumer that isn't this one composer.

F27 (parcel_gate_verdict passing owner/landUseCode rails the same day the serve reports join-hold) is read but not chased, per dispatch instruction. This lane's finding does NOT eliminate either of F27's two named mechanisms: parcel_gate_verdict gates parcel_record CELLS (a completely different store/writer than the Tier-1 bake's place_layer_snapshots + the land-use-fact atom this lane traced), so the two investigations are orthogonal.
